data.name: DeadTruth: The Dark Path Ahead
data.detailed_description:
DeadTruth is an episodic, puzzle-based, first-person horror adventure, featuring a complex and emotional story, filled with dark and mysterious secrets. DeadTruth: The Dark Path Ahead is the first episode of the DeadTruth series.

This game is based in solving puzzles. If you like games with tricky, challenging puzzles, this game is for you!

Synopsis:



You play a character named Michael Anderson who's life from loss of his loved ones, turned upside down into his worst nightmare. Despite of losing both of his parents and wife by the tragic events, another recent tragedy struck Michael's life- mysterious dissapearance of his brother Lusifer. The haunting sarrows of terrible deaths, led Michael to the dark trail of using drugs. Despite of constantly being surrounded by the never resting terror of loss and sadness, Michael finds the only spark of hope left inside of him and steps into the unknown to find his missing brother and uncover the truth behind the terrible accident.. But as further he walks into the darkness, the more he realises that the chance of life he left behind, was completly faded the moment he stepped into the shadow, as he slowly started to become the shadow himself.

Are you willing to enter the unknown?

Features:



  • Puzzle solving challenges: Horror adventure game in puzzle-like style. To challenge the player throughout the game.
  • Environmental sounds system The sounds of the different environments are contributing to the atmosphere and give the player scaring hints.
  • High quality environment: Detail graphics with chilling atmosphere and tension.
  • Sophisticated music and sounds.
  • Combat system.
  • Compelling and detailed story: Finding the answers to questions of the mysterious disappearance of your brother throughout the game. Haunting weaknesses of main characters past.
  • Interactive environments: You can interact with objects! Pick up and move around objects through a simple drag and drop interface.
  • Estimated game length: 5 - 6 hours

Caution:



DeadTruth contains violence, use of drugs, gore and strong language.

Quick note's:


It is strongly recommended to read the manual before playing the game! You can find the manual on the right side of the page.

reviews.review:
DeadTruth: The Dark Path Ahead is a first-person psychological horror adventure built around exploration, environmental puzzles, disturbing imagery, and a story driven by personal tragedy. Developed and published by BlackClothGames, the game takes a slower and more methodical approach to horror than titles centered on relentless pursuit or heavy combat. Its main appeal comes from entering oppressive locations, studying the environment for clues, manipulating objects, and gradually uncovering the mystery surrounding its troubled protagonist. The result is an ambitious indie horror experience that occasionally shows its limitations but still manages to establish an unsettling identity of its own.

The story centers on Michael Anderson, a man already carrying considerable emotional trauma before the nightmare truly begins. After losing his parents and his wife, Michael falls into drug use while attempting to cope with his grief. His life takes another disturbing turn when his brother, Lusifer, disappears. Determined to discover what happened, Michael follows a trail that leads him toward increasingly sinister circumstances. This personal motivation gives the adventure more substance than a simple haunted-location scenario, since the protagonist's grief, addiction, memories, and deteriorating psychological condition remain closely connected to the darkness surrounding him.

Exploration is fundamental to the experience. Rooms are designed to be investigated carefully rather than rushed through, and seemingly ordinary objects can have greater significance than they initially suggest. The interaction system allows players to pick up and manipulate certain items, creating a more physical approach to environmental investigation. Searching an area thoroughly is frequently necessary because important information or puzzle components can be hidden among the surroundings. This deliberate pace works particularly well when the game creates uncertainty about whether a room contains a useful clue, a threat, or something intended purely to disturb the player.

Puzzles form one of the game's defining features and are considerably more important than straightforward action. Players need to observe their surroundings, interpret clues, experiment with objects, and understand how different pieces of information connect. Some solutions can require genuine patience, making this a better fit for people who enjoy being challenged rather than immediately being shown where to go. The downside is that difficult puzzles combined with occasionally awkward interaction can interrupt the momentum. When a solution is unclear, it can sometimes be difficult to determine whether the player has overlooked a clue or simply misunderstood how an object is supposed to function.

The horror presentation relies heavily on atmosphere. Dark interiors, unsettling environmental details, carefully placed sounds, and threatening imagery create a persistent sense that something is wrong even when no immediate danger is present. Audio is particularly important because environmental sounds contribute to the tension while sometimes helping the player understand what is happening nearby. This creates several effective moments where anticipation becomes more frightening than an actual encounter. Rather than filling every corridor with obvious scares, the game often allows isolation and uncertainty to generate discomfort.

Combat exists alongside exploration and puzzle solving, giving Michael some ability to confront threats rather than remaining completely defenseless. However, action should not be mistaken for the primary attraction. The mechanics are more interesting as part of a larger mixture of horror systems than as a standalone combat experience. Movement, object manipulation, and confrontations can occasionally feel rough compared with more polished first-person horror games. These imperfections reveal the project's limited production scale, particularly when animations or interactions do not behave as smoothly as expected.

Narratively, the game attempts to connect supernatural horror with grief, addiction, loss, and psychological instability. Michael's history provides an interesting foundation because players cannot always separate the external nightmare from the protagonist's damaged mental condition. The execution can be uneven, and some dialogue or storytelling elements lack refinement, but the central mystery provides enough motivation to continue. Discovering what happened to Lusifer becomes the immediate objective, while understanding Michael himself gradually becomes another important part of the journey.

The overall experience is relatively compact, with puzzle-solving ability having a significant effect on completion time. Players who quickly understand the environmental clues can move through the adventure at a reasonable pace, while those who become stuck may spend considerably longer examining rooms and testing possible solutions. Achievement support and Steam Trading Cards add modest extras for players interested in completion. The game also contains mature material involving violence, gore, strong language, and drug-related themes, which complements its deliberately bleak tone.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially categorized as Playable rather than fully Verified. Performance with the default graphics configuration is considered suitable, and the game can run successfully on SteamOS. However, handheld players should expect compromises. Some functionality is not fully accessible through the default controller configuration, touchscreen interaction or a community controller layout may occasionally be useful, and text entry can require manually opening the virtual keyboard. Some interface text may also appear small, while certain prompts can display keyboard, mouse, or non-Steam Deck controller icons. It is therefore functional on the Deck, but the experience is less seamless than a fully optimized handheld release.

DeadTruth: The Dark Path Ahead ultimately succeeds more through atmosphere, puzzle ambition, and unsettling concepts than through technical refinement. Its combination of psychological storytelling, environmental interaction, difficult puzzles, exploration, and occasional combat gives it more mechanical substance than a passive horror walking simulator. Rough controls, uneven presentation, and some frustrating interactions hold it back, but players who enjoy obscure indie horror and are willing to accept imperfections may find its dark mystery surprisingly engaging.

Rating: 6/10
